What We Do

Full-Service Plastic Surgery Revenue Cycle Management

Plastic surgery billing requires precise distinction between reconstructive procedures covered by medical insurance and cosmetic procedures billed to the patient. PMEX categorizes every procedure correctly, documents medical necessity for reconstructive claims, and manages the full revenue cycle for both covered and self-pay services.

Reconstructive vs. Cosmetic Coding

Every procedure categorized correctly: reconstructive to insurance, cosmetic to patient billing.

Complex Wound Closure

Intermediate and complex repair codes (12031 to 13160) selected by length and complexity.

Flap Procedure Billing

Local, pedicle, and free flap CPT codes billed with correct tissue type and site.

Skin Graft Coding

Split-thickness and full-thickness graft codes billed per square centimeter from the OR report.

Breast Reconstruction

Post-mastectomy reconstruction codes billed with WHCRA compliance documentation.

Blepharoplasty Billing

Upper lid blepharoplasty coded as reconstructive when visual field testing supports coverage.

Sound Familiar?

Common Plastic Surgery Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Reconstructive procedure billed to patient as cosmetic because medical necessity not documented.

PMEX confirms medical necessity documentation is in the claim before routing reconstructive procedures to insurance.

Complex wound repair length billed below the actual measurement in the operative report.

PMEX verifies repair length from the operative report and bills the correct wound repair code per the documented centimeter measurement.

Upper lid blepharoplasty denied because visual field test results not included with the claim.

PMEX attaches visual field testing results and functional impairment documentation to every upper lid blepharoplasty claim.

Skin graft area billed at fewer square centimeters than the operative report documents.

PMEX verifies graft area from the operative report and bills per the documented square centimeters, not an estimate.

Breast reconstruction denied because WHCRA coverage notice not documented.

PMEX confirms WHCRA notice documentation is on file before billing post-mastectomy reconstruction to insurance.

Flap procedure coded at the wrong complexity level, losing the higher reconstructive reimbursement.

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm flap type (local, pedicle, or free) and codes at the correct procedure level.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Plastic Surgery Billing

Plastic surgery practices lose 16 to 28 percent of reconstructive revenue to medical necessity gaps, cosmetic vs. reconstructive misclassification, and repair measurement errors.

PATTERN 01

Upper Lid Blepharoplasty Denied, Visual Field Not Submitted

Functional upper lid blepharoplasty performed. Medical insurance claim submitted. Denied: visual field test results showing superior visual field obstruction not included. $1,200 denied per case without the supporting documentation.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX includes the visual field test results and the physician documentation of functional visual impairment with every upper lid blepharoplasty claim submitted as a reconstructive procedure.

PATTERN 02

Wound Repair Billed Below Actual Length

Laceration repair: 4.2 cm complex repair (13132, $380). Billing team submits 2.5 cm repair (13131, $240). Measurement from the operative note was not used. $140 per case under-coded from a single measurement error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX verifies the repair length from the operative report in centimeters and selects the CPT code that corresponds to the documented measurement, not the procedure superbill default.

PATTERN 03

Post-Mastectomy Reconstruction Denied, WHCRA Notice Missing

Breast reconstruction following mastectomy billed to insurance. Denied: Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act notice not documented in the patient record. Coverage is mandatory but the notice requirement was not met.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX confirms WHCRA notice documentation is on file for every post-mastectomy reconstruction patient before the claim is submitted, and tracks WHCRA compliance as a pre-billing requirement.

Questions

Plastic Surgery Billing Questions Answered

Reconstructive procedures are those performed to correct abnormal structures caused by disease, trauma, congenital abnormality, or prior surgery. Cosmetic procedures are performed to improve appearance on otherwise normal structures. We categorize from the clinical documentation and route to the correct payer.

Yes, when visual field testing documents superior visual field obstruction and the physician documents functional impairment. We include the visual field results and functional documentation with every reconstructive blepharoplasty claim.

Split-thickness and full-thickness graft codes are billed per square centimeter of graft area from the operative report. We verify the graft dimensions from the operative note before selecting the CPT code and units.

The Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act requires health plans covering mastectomy to also cover reconstruction. The plan must provide notice of this right. We confirm WHCRA notice documentation is on file before billing reconstruction to insurance.

Yes. We manage patient billing, payment plans, and collections for self-pay cosmetic procedures alongside insurance billing for reconstructive services.
